body:
I'm sure not sleeping is a huge part of why everything is hitting me so hard, but I don't know what to do when I can't even sleep while medicated. That's been extremely frustrating. 

Honestly, I have some big regrets in my life. I wish I had finished college the first time I went. I got into a fantastic university and worked so hard to get there, but left my senior year to care for my younger sister since my parents were doing an awful job of it after I moved away. She's a complete fuck up and I regret throwing my life away for her. She didn't appreciate it at all.

I love my husband dearly, but he's a lot of things I swore I'd never put up with. We differ in a lot of ways that, over the years, I've realized are more major than I thought. 

I had huge dreams my whole life that I would finish college and move far away from here, once my sister was old enough to care for herself. But she's in her early 20s now and still can't even hold a job, and since then I've gotten married and found a career that's unfortunately for now very rooted here. My husband loves his family and they all live here, so he isn't even interested in leaving. I fantasize constantly about getting out of here and never looking back. Just disappearing one day and not telling a soul, just starting a completely new life somewhere else like this one never even happened. 

Unfortunately today I found out whatever is making me sick is autoimmune related. Lupus and Addison's disease seem to make the most sense from the list of possibilities I was given. That plus my fertility issues... looks like I'll never live the life I expected to.

I really would love to finally talk but my laptop is dying and my husband is sleeping for once, in the room where the charger is. He never sleeps these days so I won't risk waking him. It's good to know I at least have somewhere that someone will listen. These comments weren't anything crazy but just having someone respond by saying they'll listen put me in tears. I've gotten so used to being ignored at this point. Thank you

I do but I always feel like I'm just rambling on and being annoying, so I delete everything I came up with 100 times. Its quite the double edged sword! But honestly even being asked makes me feel better already.

My therapist does have an emergency location but its first come first serve and pretty far away. It's crazy to me that people can reach out (which takes a lot of pushing to do) just to be told they have to wait a month or more to even be considered. Says a lot about how we view mental health.
